requirements.description: put() must atomically check capacity AND add the message (no TOCTOU race)
evidence: queue.py put() (lines 29-40): capacity check and append both inside `with self._lock` (threading.Lock mutex)
No TOCTOU window: the lock is acquired before the check and released after the append

requirements.description: get() must use an acknowledgment pattern — messages not removed until consumer explicitly acknowledges
evidence: queue.py get() returns (message, receipt) tuple; message stored in self._in_flight dict — not deleted
ack() deletes from in_flight; nack() pops and re-queues via appendleft at front
Receipt: str(uuid.uuid4()) — unique token per message
consumer.py run_once(): on success → ack(receipt); on exception → nack(receipt) + re-raise
All queue methods protected by self._lock
Verified by: test_nack_requeues_message, test_acked_message_not_redelivered, test_multiple_in_flight_nack_all, test_concurrent_no_message_loss

requirements.description: Priority queue must use a deterministic, type-safe tie-breaker for equal-priority messages
evidence: priority.py PriorityTask: urgency=int (primary), seq=int (tie-breaker), message=Any with field(compare=False)
message excluded from comparison — safe for dict/list/any payload

requirements.description: All tests must pass: pytest tests/
evidence: 6 test modules: test_single_thread.py (6), test_concurrent.py (2), test_capacity.py (2), test_message_loss.py (1), test_crash_recovery.py (3), test_ordering.py (3)

requirements.description: Handle 10,000 messages across 20 concurrent threads with zero loss
evidence: Producers retry with QueueFull backoff; consumers use ack pattern

notes: Independent verification — no coordination with verifier2
Minor note: put() capacity check counts len(self._queue) only, not in-flight. is_full() sums both. Consistency note, not a spec violation.
